sections.model_projection: The model projects the Los Angeles Rams to win 28.75 to 21.66, a home margin of 7.09 points and a combined total of 50.41. The Rams are given a 71.5% win probability. Note that this game is played at a neutral site (Melbourne Cricket Ground), so no traditional home-field advantage is applied. The model's projected margin of 7.1 points is 3.6 points larger than the market spread of Rams -3.5, and the projected total of 50.4 sits 1.9 points above the market total of 48.5.
sections.offensive_matchup: The Rams enter as the model's top-ranked offense, posting an EPA per play (a measure of how many expected points each play adds) of 0.208 and a 51.7% offensive success rate — both ranked 1st — against a 49ers defense that ranks 25th in defensive EPA per play allowed (0.071) and 28th in defensive success rate allowed (48.1%). That defensive vulnerability means the Rams should find consistent gains on a high share of their snaps. San Francisco's offense is legitimately strong in its own right, ranking 3rd in offensive EPA per play (0.137) and 2nd in offensive success rate (50.3%), but it runs into a Rams defense that ranks 11th in defensive EPA per play (-0.027), a meaningful step up in resistance. The Rams' offense generates 6.44 yards per play (1st) against a 49ers defense allowing 5.59 yards per play (20th), reinforcing the structural advantage Los Angeles holds in this matchup.
sections.quarterback_edge: Brock Purdy holds the edge in career efficiency metrics: his career EPA per dropback (a per-play value-added measure for quarterbacks) is 0.204 versus Matthew Stafford's 0.131, and his career yards per attempt is 8.51 versus Stafford's 7.73. However, Stafford has 84 career games with 10-plus attempts compared to Purdy's 53, giving him a larger experience base, and Stafford is listed as a returning starter while Purdy carries a new-starter-same-team flag. The model scores this edge slightly in Purdy's favor (-0.39 points toward the Rams), making it the smallest of the quarterback-related factors. Both quarterbacks have zero season attempts logged, so this assessment rests entirely on career data.
sections.trenches: The offensive line matchup is the single largest driver in the model, worth 1.15 points toward the Rams. Los Angeles ranks 1st in line yards per rush (3.41, a metric crediting the offensive line specifically for run-blocking) and 3rd in sack rate allowed (3.9%), while allowing pressure on only 18.7% of dropbacks (6th). They face a 49ers defensive front that ranks 32nd in pressure rate (16.4%) and 32nd in havoc rate (the share of plays producing a sack, TFL, forced fumble, or turnover, at 11.6%), meaning San Francisco's pass rush generates almost no disruption without the blitz. Conversely, San Francisco's offensive line is solid — ranking 4th in sack rate allowed (4.3%) and 8th in pressure rate allowed (18.9%) — but faces a Rams defensive front that generates pressure on 27.9% of dropbacks without blitzing at a 15.7% rate (5th), giving Los Angeles a credible pass-rush threat. The run-blocking gap is equally stark: the Rams' line yards of 3.41 (1st) against a 49ers run defense allowing a line yards figure of 2.99 (24th) points to Los Angeles controlling the ground game.
sections.explosive_play_edge: The Rams hold a clear explosive-play advantage, ranking 1st in explosive play rate at 12.25% (plays gaining 10-plus rushing or 20-plus passing yards) against a 49ers defense that allows explosives on 7.36% of plays (4th-best). San Francisco's offense generates explosives on only 8.54% of plays (17th), and while their defense is excellent at limiting big plays (4th), the Rams' explosiveness rating of 1.17 (a measure of big-play magnitude) is the highest in the model. The net result is a moderate edge favoring the Rams in this category, worth 0.23 points, as Los Angeles is more likely to break the game open with chunk plays than San Francisco.
sections.third_down_red_zone: Third down is San Francisco's clearest structural advantage in this game: the 49ers convert at a 51.1% rate (1st in the league) while the Rams convert at only 38.2% (22nd), and the model scores this edge at -3 favoring the 49ers — the strongest single-category edge in their favor. In the red zone, the Rams hold a slight edge, scoring touchdowns on 67.4% of trips (6th) and earning 3.74 points per scoring opportunity (1st), compared to San Francisco's 65.6% red-zone touchdown rate (8th) and 3.45 points per scoring opportunity (2nd). The 49ers' red-zone defense is better, allowing touchdowns on only 56.7% of opponent trips (11th) versus the Rams' 61.0% (20th), so San Francisco can limit damage when the Rams reach the red zone — but the Rams' superior efficiency at converting scoring opportunities into maximum points gives them a narrow overall edge there.
sections.roster_talent: The Rams carry a continuity index of 0.96 — meaning 96% of their roster production returns — with 100% of passing and receiving production back and 98% of rushing production. San Francisco's continuity index is 0.68, with only 69% of receiving production and 65% of defensive production returning. The Rams also return 78 offensive line starts versus the 49ers' 72. This returning-production edge is worth 0.52 points toward the Rams in the model. Talent ratings are unavailable for both teams, so no further assessment can be made on that dimension.
sections.recent_form: Both teams have played zero games in the 2026 season, and the model records a form shift of 0.0 for each team. There is no recent in-season performance data to evaluate. All metrics carry a low-sample flag and are drawn from prior-season blended data. The recent form category is scored as neutral.
sections.market_movement: The spread has held at Rams -3.5 since the first recorded snapshot on DraftKings, with zero movement across 162 snapshots on nine books. The total has similarly held at 48.5 with no movement. The moneyline has shifted modestly from Rams -198 to -185 (and 49ers +164 to +154), a slight drift toward the 49ers on the moneyline without any spread movement. No book disagreement on the spread is recorded. Public ticket and money percentages are unavailable, so no claim about the source of any movement can be made.
key_advantages: Rams offensive line dominates both pass protection (3rd in sack rate allowed) and run blocking (1st in line yards) against a 49ers defensive front ranked last in pressure rate and havoc rate
Rams offense ranks 1st in EPA per play, success rate, yards per play, and explosive play rate against a 49ers defense ranked 25th in EPA allowed and 28th in success rate allowed
Rams turnover margin of +0.70 per game (2nd) versus 49ers turnover margin of -0.68 per game (30th) represents a significant ball-security edge
Rams roster continuity of 96% versus 49ers 68% gives Los Angeles a substantial returning-production advantage heading into Week 1
key_concerns: San Francisco's 51.1% third-down conversion rate (1st) against the Rams' 38.7% third-down defense rate (12th) means the 49ers can sustain drives and keep the Rams offense off the field
Brock Purdy's career EPA per dropback of 0.204 outpaces Stafford's 0.131, and the 49ers' passing offense ranks 3rd in EPA per pass play against a Rams pass defense ranked only 13th
San Francisco's defense limits explosive plays on only 7.36% of opponent plays (4th-best), which could cap the Rams' big-play ceiling despite their 1st-ranked explosive rate
sections.expected_game_script: The Rams are expected to establish control early by leveraging their top-ranked offensive line and run-blocking unit against a 49ers defensive front that generates almost no pressure or havoc. Los Angeles should move the ball consistently — their 51.7% offensive success rate against San Francisco's 48.1% defensive success rate allowed creates a persistent down-and-distance advantage — and their play-action rate of 30.9% (3rd) pairs well against a 49ers defense that struggles to generate pressure without the blitz. San Francisco will keep the game competitive through their elite third-down conversion ability (51.1%), which allows them to sustain long drives and limit the Rams' possessions, and Purdy's efficiency should produce points when the 49ers do move the ball. However, the Rams' turnover margin edge (+0.70 vs. -0.68) introduces a meaningful risk of the 49ers giving the ball away at critical moments, which could accelerate the Rams' scoring. The model projects a final score of 28.75 to 21.66, consistent with a game where the Rams build a two-score lead in the second half but the 49ers' third-down efficiency keeps them within striking distance throughout. The neutral site at Melbourne Cricket Ground removes any crowd-noise factor, leaving the structural matchup edges as the primary determinants of the outcome.
